title: Text 2
subtitle: 学位的价值与Z世代的选择

sentences.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
sentences.zh: 当最新一届学生填写大学本科入学申请表并权衡各种选择时，或许值得思考一下：学位的意义、目的和价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，以及Z世代在开启教育之旅的第三阶段时需要考虑些什么。

sentences.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life.
sentences.zh: 千禧一代曾被告知，只要在学校表现出色、拿到一份体面的学位，这辈子就有着落了。

sentences.en: But that promise has been found wanting.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这一承诺并不牢靠。

sentences.en: As degrees became universal, they became devalued.
sentences.zh: 随着学位的普及，学位也随之贬值了。

sentences.en: Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility.
sentences.zh: 教育不再是实现社会流动的可靠途径。

sentences.en: Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among OECD countries.
sentences.zh: 如今，英国有28%的毕业生从事的是不需要学位的岗位，这一比例是经合组织国家平均水平的两倍。

sentences.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说获得学位毫无意义，而是要强调：学位并非适合所有人，从中学课堂到大学讲堂的转变并非必然的选择，而且还有其他选择可供考虑。

sentences.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
sentences.zh: 值得庆幸的是，已有迹象表明这种情况正在发生：Z世代正试图向千禧一代前辈学习，尽管家长和老师们往往仍固守着“学位至上”的观念。

sentences.en: Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates.
sentences.zh: 雇主们早就看到了雇佣中学毕业后直接进入职场者的好处，这些人往往被证明比大学毕业生更敬业、更忠诚。

sentences.en: Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
sentences.zh: 也有许多雇主认识到，取消某些职位的学位要求是有好处的。

sentences.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many.
sentences.zh: 对于那些把攻读学位作为理想路径的人来说，不妨想一想：这很可能只是众多阶段中的第一个。

sentences.en: In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.
sentences.zh: 在这个通才的时代，拥有专门的知识或技能是值得的。

sentences.en: Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates.
sentences.zh: 如今，研究生的收入比本科生高出40%。

sentences.en: When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
sentences.zh: 当越来越多的人拥有本科学位时，再拿一个学位就合情合理了。

sentences.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay employable.
sentences.zh: Z世代不太可能在18岁或21岁就结束学业；为了保持就业竞争力，他们将需要在整个职业生涯中不断学习新技能。

sentences.en: It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers.
sentences.zh: 据估计，由于技术的压力、对个人成就感的追求以及多样性的渴望，这一代人将在整个职业生涯中为17个不同的雇主工作，并从事5种不同的职业。

sentences.en: Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z’s career trajectory.
sentences.zh: 教育——不仅仅是校园里学到的知识——将成为Z世代职业发展轨迹的核心组成部分。

sentences.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: ‘I am a geographer’ or ‘I am a classist’.
sentences.zh: 老一辈人常常用现在时、以个人身份来谈论自己的学位：“我是一名地理学家”或“我是一名古典学家”。

sentences.en: Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it’s as if they already know that their degree won’t define them in the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们的儿女绝不会说出这样的话；他们似乎已经知道，学位不会再像从前那样定义他们的人生。

questions.stem: The author suggests that Generation Z should ______.

options.A: be careful in choosing a college
options.B: be diligent at each educational stage
options.C: reassess the necessity of college education

questions.analysis: 首段即提出值得重新审视学位的意义、价值以及 Z 世代的选择；第二段又指出学位贬值、不再是可靠的社会流动途径，故建议 Z 世代重新评估大学教育的必要性。

questions.stem: The percentage of UK graduates in non-graduate roles reflect ______.

options.B: the shrinking value of a degree
options.D: the desired route of social mobility

questions.analysis: 第二段以英国 28% 毕业生从事非毕业生岗位为例，说明“学位变得普遍后价值被稀释”（As degrees became universal, they became devalued），即反映学位价值缩水。

questions.stem: The author considers it a good sign that ______.

options.A: Generation Z are seeking to earn a decent degree
options.B: school leavers are willing to be skilled workers
options.C: employers are taking a realistic attitude to degrees
options.D: parents are changing their minds about education

questions.analysis: 第三、四段称雇主早已看到招聘离校生的好处，并开始取消部分岗位的学位要求，这是好迹象，即雇主对学位态度趋于现实。

questions.stem: It is advised in Paragraph 5 that those with one degree should ______.

options.A: make an early decision on their career
options.B: attend on the job training programs
options.D: further their studies in a specific field

questions.analysis: 第五段建议：在已有学位的基础上，最好再具备特定知识或技能（in this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills），即继续深造某一领域。

questions.stem: What can be concluded about Generation Z from the last two paragraphs?

options.C: Degrees will no longer appeal them.
options.D: They will have a limited choice of jobs.

questions.analysis: 末两段指出 Z 世代将不断“提升技能”（up-skilling）以保持可就业性，教育将成为其职业轨迹的核心部分，说明终身学习将定义他们。
